patch_description:
The original program was broken in several fundamental ways: (1) it returned an empty list `[]` as `column_orderings`, so per-row column orderings were invalid/missing; (2) it fabricated an "original_index" helper column, merged/sorted rows with pandas merge (which can reorder/duplicate rows and coerce dtypes), and its recursive path reconstructed DataFrames from value lists, altering dtypes and row identity; (3) its recursion used heuristics (squared string lengths, `itertuples` attribute access on arbitrary labels) that frequently crashed or diverged from the actual objective (character-Trie prefix reuse).

The fix replaces the whole editable block with a correct, bounded implementation aligned with the real objective: serialize cells (missing → ""), build a small set of candidate per-row column orderings — (a) global ordering ranked by sum len(v)*count(v)*(count(v)-1), (b) frequency-ranked ordering, and (c) a bounded conditional partition tree that picks a leading field per group by length-weighted pair repetition and recurses on partitions — then score each candidate exactly with the ideal Trie reuse (sum of adjacent LCPs of the sorted serialized rows, computed via C-speed binary search on prefix slices), and output the best. It preserves every cell value and the exact number of rows/columns, honors col_merge via the existing merging_columns API, enforces one_way_dep precedence by swapping positions, pushes highly distinct columns (per distinct_value_threshold) to the tail, and returns a valid per-row `column_orderings` list consistent with the returned object-dtype DataFrame.
